title: 11 Best Herbal Creams For Peripheral Arterial Occlusive Disease
intro: Herbal creams for Peripheral arterial occlusive disease are topical preparations made from plant extracts that are used to alleviate symptoms and improve circulation in individuals suffering from this condition, characterized by the narrowing of blood vessels in the limbs due to atherosclerosis. These creams have been found to provide several benefits, including improved blood flow, reduced inflammation, and enhanced wound healing. Examples of herbal creams used to treat peripheral arterial occlusive disease include those containing ginkgo biloba, which improves circulation by dilating blood vessels, and those containing horse chestnut, which reduces inflammation and edema in the affected limbs. Other herbal creams, such as those containing saw palmetto, turmeric, and cayenne pepper, are also used to treat this condition, as they help to improve circulation, reduce pain, and prevent the progression of the disease.

preparations.preparation_desc: Ginkgo biloba creams have been studied for their potential to treat peripheral arterial occlusive disease, a condition characterized by reduced blood flow to the limbs. The anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties of Ginkgo biloba help to improve blood circulation, which in turn alleviates symptoms of the condition. The bioactive constituents, including flavonoids and terpenoids, work to dilate blood vessels and reduce platelet aggregation, thereby enhancing blood flow to the affected areas. By using Ginkgo biloba creams, patients with peripheral arterial occlusive disease may experience improved mobility, reduced pain, and enhanced overall quality of life.
preparations.preparation_study: According to "Zhongguo yao li xue bao = Acta pharmacologica Sinica", Ginkgo biloba creams for peripheral arterial occlusive disease were found to improve the pain-free walking distance by a factor of 3.8 times in diabetic patients and 3.3 times in nondiabetic patients after 48 weeks of treatment.

preparations.preparation_desc: Panax ginseng creams have been explored for their potential in treating peripheral arterial occlusive disease (PAOD), a condition characterized by reduced blood flow to the limbs. The bioactive constituents of Panax ginseng, including ginsenosides and saponins, have been found to help alleviate symptoms of PAOD by improving blood circulation and reducing inflammation. The antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties of these compounds aid in protecting the vascular endothelium and promoting the growth of new blood vessels, thus facilitating the treatment of PAOD. The use of Panax ginseng creams may help to alleviate symptoms of PAOD, such as pain and fatigue, and improve overall quality of life for individuals suffering from this condition.
preparations.preparation_study: According to "Journal of ethnopharmacology", Panax ginseng creams for peripheral arterial occlusive disease may be beneficial due to the presence of ginsenoside Rg1, which has been shown to inhibit vascular intimal hyperplasia by reducing the expression of certain axes, such as SDF-1α/CXCR4, SCF/c-kit, and FKN/CX3CR1, thus potentially alleviating symptoms of the disease.

intro_study: According to "Annales Academiae Medicae Stetinensis", creams for peripheral arterial occlusive disease using bioflavonoides, salicylates, valepotriates, tannins, phenol acids, ethereal oils, and esters of acids found in preparations like PADMA-28 may be beneficial, as these components collectively contribute to the positive effects observed in patients with intermittent claudication.
